greeting: Rawr, hello! I'm Saagar's dragon. Ask me about his work, services, rates or how to reach him.
fallback: That one's outside my cave. I only know what's on this site: Saagar's work, services, products and how to reach him. Try asking about those, or write to him directly.

intents.a: Hello, traveller! I guard this site and know my way around it. What would you like to know about Saagar?

I'm the pixel dragon who flies around Saagar's nav bar. I'm not a big language model; I answer from this site's own pages, so I won't make things up. The dragon art is original, and you may use it with a credit line.

Saagar Shrestha is a UX design engineer in Kathmandu. He blends AI, UX design and frontend engineering, and has shipped 100+ projects over 10+ years: end-to-end UX, interface design and design systems for startups and product teams.

q: what can you do for me
intents.a: Saagar offers user research, rapid prototyping, UX audits and strategy, design systems, end-to-end product design, frontend builds and 2D animation. He also slots into existing design teams for audits or hands-on interface work.
Yes, Saagar is available for work, with limited capacity. He takes on a small number of projects at a time so each one gets proper attention. The contact page is the fastest way to start.
Saagar works mostly by the hour at $25–35/hour, or a fixed monthly price for ongoing work. The rate is agreed before work starts. Tell him what you need and he'll send a proposal.
Email saagarshrest@gmail.com. Saagar reads it himself and replies. For short messages, WhatsApp +977-9860332656 works too.
Sure. Saagar's on WhatsApp at +977-9860332656. Keep it short; email is better for anything detailed.

Saagar is based in Kathmandu, Nepal, and works remotely with clients across time zones. Calls, shared design files and short written briefs do most of the work; a weekly overlap for a sync is usually enough.

q: how long does a project take
intents.a: A focused UX audit or design system sprint usually takes two to four weeks. Full product engagements run longer and are split into phases, so you see value early.

Saagar has worked in product design since 2016. Most recently he was Senior Product Designer at Ad Leverage, and before that he worked at Signetic, IDA, Dreamax, Bitsbeat, Healent, Braindigit, Floyd and Blackspring. The resume has the full timeline.

His toolkit: Figma, Framer, Adobe, After Effects and Lottie for design and motion; HTML, CSS and Tailwind for building; Jira for delivery; Claude and ChatGPT for AI-assisted work. He designs and codes, so handoff isn't an issue.
Case studies: Harmony Wallet, Field Service Ops (HVAC), Officiti, Simple Period Tracker, ShiftCare and Ramroparts. Each one covers the problem, the process and the outcome.

Design systems are one of Saagar's specialities. The Design System page shows the Officiti system for iOS and Android, and his free DesignSystem Creator generates tokens and checks contrast against WCAG 2.2.

A UX audit takes two to four weeks. Saagar scores every screen and flow against Nielsen's ten usability heuristics and the Laws of UX, then hands over prioritised fixes. The UX Audit page shows how he runs one.
His resume covers experience since 2016, an EMBA, certifications and tools. You can download it as a PDF from the resume page.
Saagar holds the Google Project Management certificate (2023), the Google UX Design certificate (2022) and a Digital Marketing certification (2018), plus an EMBA.

All the products are free and run in your browser, with no account and no uploads. They include DesignSystem Creator, Image Cleaner, the Free UI/UX Design Academy, Simple Period Tracker and two games. Saagar built them with AI.
There are two pixel games: Coin Commando and Kathmandu Shadows. Both are free and play in the browser.
The Store sells the Pink Petal Planner for $1 on Gumroad.
Saagar writes his own articles on accessibility, emotional design, design thinking, data versus intuition, and AI in UX. Some are also published on Medium.
Saagar has worked with 42 clients, from startups to established product teams. The Clients page lists them.

Yes. AI is part of how Saagar works: research, prototyping and building with tools like Claude and ChatGPT. All the free products here were built with AI. He's also written about why AI needs good UX.
